target_customer: Women in their late 20s and 30s who want to freeze their eggs and pay out of pocket
problem: Egg freezing is expensive (about 15,000 dollars at a standard clinic per the company site) and confusing to navigate, so many women delay or never do it.
business_model: Concierge service for egg freezing; fixed price package with partner clinics (site listed 9,500 dollars with medications included, 10,500 in NYC)

founders.name: Alyssa Atkins
founders.background_notes: Alumna of the NEXT 36 program in 2013 per NEXT Canada (August 2019). Froze her own eggs at 29 per the company site. Prior employers and education not found in an opened source. The YC page lists her as the only founder.

competitors.name: Extend Fertility
competitors.what: Egg freezing clinic in New York offering lower cost cycles
competitors.traction_then: Overseen nearly 2,000 egg freezing cycles since 2016 per a 2020 piece
competitors.funding_then: 15 million dollars Series A in 2019 per Well + Good

competitors.name: Kindbody
competitors.funding_then: 15 million dollars Series A in 2019 per Well + Good

technical_complexity.rationale: A concierge layer on top of existing clinics; the work was operations, clinic partnerships and marketing, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Clinic partnerships and a founder-led brand were the only assets; clinics or better funded rivals such as Kindbody and Extend could offer the same pricing.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Funded clinic chains already marketed lower cost egg freezing in 2019 and 2020. No source shows they copied Lilia specifically.

market_need_then: High clinic prices and confusing medical terminology; the founder cited a three month wait for fertility test results and confusion about terms as her motivation (NEXT Canada, August 2019).

branding.domain_note: Used hellolilia.com, a prefix domain, not the exact .com

identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and empowering; the founder prefers the phrase egg securing; tagline 'Your Egg Freezing Concierge' and 'For women by women'

branding.brand_signature: Founder as the face of the brand; she hosted what she called the first egg freezing celebration
branding.community_and_virality: Press mentions listed on the site (Elle, Vogue, Forbes), podcast interviews with the founder; no merch or fan community found

brand_strength.rationale: Some press and podcast coverage tied to the founder, but the name is a common first name and spelling appears as both Lilia and Lillia in third party pages; no sign the brand drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Lilia raised about 2.2 million dollars across a 2019 pre-seed and a 2020 seed and built a small concierge business with hundreds of clients, yet YC lists it as Inactive and no source states the cause. The model was services heavy with low defensibility against funded clinic chains, and the founder reportedly stepped away, but the cause of the inactive status is not public. The failure factor is a weak inference from the lack of any later round and should be read with that caveat.
notes: Cause of Inactive status not found in public sources. The 1.4 million seed with named investors rests on a single database (Seedtable, citing PitchBook); a healthcare directory repeats it without a primary source. Aggregators put total raised at 2.2 to 2.35 million, consistent with the two rounds. A February 2022 secondary transaction reported by PitchBook is not recorded as a round. Crunchbase round data was unreliable. The site footer said Toronto while YC says San Francisco and New York.
